Commenter comparing open-source alternatives: "Agreed that LaunchDarkly is incredibly over priced."
"I have used LaunchDarkly in the past and yeah it's kind of a pain to use."
User reports their logs show frequent timeouts when looking up settings through LaunchDarkly's API, noting the SDK default timeout is 3s and they wouldn't want to wait longer.

Critic calls outsourcing feature flags to a third party a questionable architecture: it creates a critical-path hard dependency that most apps hit multiple times per request and would rather run locally.

Lanetix user: used LaunchDarkly for about a year after a homegrown flag library built by their CTO. LD provided a lot more and keeps releasing features that would have been much more expensive to build than buy. Most of the LD implementation was done in a 24-hour hackathon.

Upserve engineer and avid LD user: product managers outside engineering can control who gets features without a dev console. Rules-based targeting lets them set a flag at the restaurant-group level and have it propagate to users. Percentage and attribute rollouts (e.g. 10% of users in Rhode Island) are also supported.

Upserve user: flags are used across dozens of components and thousands of agents on customer hardware. LD streams changes via server-sent events, adding no extra latency for network calls. This gave them confidence to use flags anywhere. Multivariate flags let them throttle agent data (1MB/5MB/10MB per batch).

Upserve user values LD's prerequisite/chained flags for 'big bang' launches and its analytics for spotting stale flags and marking temporary vs permanent ones to reduce tech debt. A Slack integration posts flag changes to their #product channel, cutting communication overhead.
Commenter says that for teams wanting to merge and release regularly and make launches easy, LaunchDarkly is a big win, though you can also build feature toggles yourself with open-source libraries.
Skeptic: "In the production systems I've worked on this is literally 25 lines of code," calling feature-flag-as-a-service a shark-jumping moment.

Block/Square engineer with lots of LaunchDarkly experience: a real value-add of LD is what it does with evaluation data apps send upstream, flagging unused flags, flags only ever evaluated to the default, or to one outcome. LD's open-source Relay lets you run proxies closer to your services.

Same engineer: LD clients download all flags in the project on connection, then stream changes. LD's rule system (ordered rules with ANDed conditions over arbitrary contexts) is arguably better than their internal expression language. Many open-source options are more limited.

LaunchDarkly has a mobile client SDK, but it charges by MAU, which would be untenable, so folks tend to write their own server-side proxy that evaluates flags with the server SDK and returns them to mobile apps.

User praises LD's "Code References" feature for answering "where is this flag used in code?". They note LD's Big Segments fetch segment inclusion live from Redis (then cache), rather than purely local evaluation.
User finds LaunchDarkly's "comparison with Split" page and Split's "comparison with LaunchDarkly" page amusing, especially when they make the exact same evaluations in reverse.
